supports.interpretation: Real external footprint exists via ExOne 10-Ks (the IP-license counterparty). However, none of the 6 named OEM customers (Daimler/BMW/Ford/VW/Porsche/Evonik) appears to disclose voxeljet in their EDGAR filings. For US-listed counterparties, this is consistent with vendor-of-vendor scale (foundry tooling), not direct material relationships.

C1.interpretation: Customer names are real companies and the additive-manufacturing relationship is plausible (foundry/sand 3D printing for engine prototyping is well-documented in trade press). But the framework cannot independently corroborate any of the 6 named OEM customers via their own US filings — only the IP-license counterparty (ExOne) leaves a footprint. Apply foreign-issuer calibration: 1-3 mentions of foreign counterparties (BMW ADR, VW, Porsche) is normal; 0 from US-listed Ford is also expected for a small-vendor relationship. Calibrated as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED_FLAG: claim is plausible but lacks independent corroboration at the asserted granularity.

supports.interpretation: Zero EPA-FRS-registered facilities in Michigan named voxeljet. Per calibration heuristic: US service center is light assembly + on-demand parts (binder-jet powder bed); the German plant required emissions permit due to resin use, but US service center may operate at smaller scale below US permitting thresholds. Plausible foreign-issuer treatment: light-industrial 3D-print service centers commonly fly below EPA FRS.

C2.interpretation: EPA FRS does not list a voxeljet MI facility. Apply calibration heuristic 1: light assembly / R&D / on-demand parts services are plausibly NOT EPA-permitted in the US. Without an alternative US registry source for industrial-tenant verification, this is UNVERIFIABLE rather than RED_FLAG.

C3.interpretation: USPTO ODP shows 60 granted patents pre-cutoff with at least one match in claimed categories ({'binder_jet': 6, 'printer_apparatus': 62, 'materials': 2}). Real portfolio exists.

supports.interpretation: Stratasys does not mention voxeljet. Stratasys' principal market is FDM/PolyJet (plastic prototyping); voxeljet's principal market is binder-jet sand for foundry casting — different end markets explain non-mention.

Among additive-manufacturing US-listed peers, only ExOne (the binder-jet competitor with overlapping IP) discusses voxeljet — the technology overlap that triggers IP licensing IS the same overlap that drives competitive disclosure.

C8.interpretation: MODERATE — voxeljet does have an external US filer footprint (ExOne) but missing in Stratasys/3D Systems is consistent with non-overlapping product segments. Niche binder-jet sand-printing for foundry casting is not Stratasys' arena.
